info.name: QH Connectathon Track 2: Radiology Referral
info.description:
Requests for the FHIR in Queensland Health Connectathon, Track 2 (FHIR for Services): discover an imaging service, create a referral, triage, book and track.

1. Import this collection and one of the two environments.
2. Run the folders in order (1 to 6; 6 is a stretch), or use the Collection Runner. Folder 9 cleans up what you created.
3. Read the guide: https://aehrc.github.io/qh-connectathon/track2/QH-Track2-API-Guide.html

All data is fictional. Pre-seeded ids (`qhd-*` directory, `qhc-*` referral) are used as defaults, so every folder also works on its own.

item.name: 1 Discover (Provider Directory)
item.description: Scenario step 1, test cases D-01 to D-03 and X-01. Targets the **directory** server (`{{directoryUrl}}`). Every request carries `X-Request-ID` (set by the collection pre-request script). Search parameters are Day-1 assumptions until the ADHA HCPD technical specification is published.

request.description: Find CT services in Queensland and bring back the Location and Organization in the same Bundle. 310128004 = Computed tomography service. Saves the first HealthcareService id for the next requests.
Request a small page, then copy `Bundle.link[relation=next].url` into your client. The test stores the next link in `{{nextPageUrl}}`; use the 'Follow next link' request.
Follows the `next` link saved by the previous request.

item.name: D-02 Resolve service, organization and endpoints

request.description: One round trip from the chosen HealthcareService to its Organization, Location and **Endpoint** resources. Read `Endpoint.address` and `Endpoint.payloadType` to learn how to reach the receiving server. Note: the seeded `Endpoint.address` values are in-cluster URLs (`*.svc.cluster.local`), so use the public referral URL from the environment instead.
Endpoint has no `organization` search parameter in R4. Reach it through the owning resource with `_include`.

item.name: D-02 Locations in a town, with their services

request.description: Location search by town, with every HealthcareService that is delivered there.
Look up practitioner roles for an organisation. HPI-I is on the Practitioner identifier, HPI-O on the Organization identifier.
Asynchronous bulk export of the CT services. Expect `202 Accepted` with a `Content-Location` header. The test saves it in `{{exportStatusUrl}}`.
`202` while running (honour `Retry-After`), `200` with an `output[].url` list when finished. Download each `url` as NDJSON.

item.name: 2 Create the referral (Referral Server)
item.description: Scenario step 2, test cases R-01 and R-02. Targets the **referral** server (`{{referralUrl}}`).

request.description: Smoke check that the referral server is up and shows its FHIR version.

One transaction creating Patient, eGFR Observation, ServiceRequest, the Group Task and the fulfilment Task, linked with `urn:uuid:` references. The referrer is `PractitionerRole/qhc-role-1` and the receiving service is the seeded Tropic Coast Health Service. All resources are tagged with `{{runId}}` so you can clean up. The ids of what was created are saved to collection variables for the following requests.

exec: // remembered separately so folder 9 can only ever delete what this run created, never seeded data
// the second Task in the Bundle is the fulfilment Task

item.name: R-01 Validate the ServiceRequest against the IG

request.description: Asks the server to validate a ServiceRequest against `referral-servicerequest`. Errors fail the test; warnings are fine. (Tip: the profile is claimed in `meta.profile`.)

item.name: R-02 Referral with its supporting information

request.description: Reads back the referral you created, with the eGFR Observation and Patient in the same Bundle. A contrast study should always carry an eGFR.
The server is pre-loaded with 22 fictional referrals for 20 patients. Use these if you only want to read.

item.name: 3 Triage (Imaging Provider / filler)
item.description: Scenario step 3, test cases T-01 and T-02. The filler finds new work and moves the Task through its states. These use JSON Patch so you do not need to resend the whole Task.

item.name: T-01 Find new work for a filler

request.description: New Tasks for one filler organisation, with the focus ServiceRequest. Seeded filler: `qhc-org-fill1`. Note: the Group Task has no `focus`; the fulfilment Task does.
Task `requested` to `accepted`. Run request R-01 first so `{{taskId}}` is set.

item.name: T-02 Put on hold with a coded reason

request.description: Variant: `on-hold` with a `statusReason`, as in the contrast-allergy storyline ('contrast allergy, please confirm'). Resend the Accept request afterwards to continue the flow.
Variant: `rejected`. Use on a throwaway referral, because a rejected Task is final.

item.name: 4 Availability and booking
item.description: Scenario steps 4 and 5, test cases B-01 to B-04. Run **2 Create the referral** first. The server does **not** stop two Appointments being created against one Slot, so a booking client must re-read the Slot and check `status=free` immediately before it books (see B-03).

request.description: A Schedule for a CT service. Uses a client-assigned id so the call is idempotent.

item.name: B-01 Filler publishes a free Slot

request.description: A 30 minute free Slot, one week from now.

exec: const d = new Date(); d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + 7); d.setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
const iso = h => new Date(d.getTime() + h * 3600e3).toISOString();

request.description: Free Slots for the schedule, from today, by service type. To search a seeded provider instead use `schedule=Schedule/qhc-sched-f1-ct` or `schedule.actor=HealthcareService/qhc-hcs-f1-ct` (seeded slots are free on 4 and 5 Nov 2026).
Creates a `proposed` Appointment on the Slot, linked to the ServiceRequest through `basedOn`.
Appointment `proposed` to `booked`.
Slot `free` to `busy`. This is the filler's job; the server does not do it for you.

item.name: B-02 Filler confirms: Task in-progress / booked

request.description: Task to `in-progress` with business status `service-booked`. If you ran an on-hold or reject request, re-run **R-01** for a fresh Task.

item.name: B-03 Check the Slot before booking (taken Slot)

request.description: After B-02 the Slot is `busy`. A well behaved referrer reads it and stops here. Creating a second Appointment against this Slot would currently succeed (no server-side conflict check), so the check belongs in your client.
Appointment to `cancelled`, with a cancellation reason.
Slot back to `free`.

item.name: B-04 Rebook on a second Slot

request.description: Publishes a second free Slot an hour later; then re-run **B-02 Referrer proposes an Appointment** after pointing `{{slotId}}` at it (set it in the collection variables).

item.name: 5 Track status
item.description: Scenario step 6, test case S-01. The referrer reads the Task and Appointment and displays status and businessStatus.

item.name: S-01 Task state for the referral

request.description: The fulfilment Task for the referral. After the B-02 confirmations it reads `in-progress` / `service-booked`.
All Appointments raised against the referral, any status.
Read-only: appointments already booked in the seed data (`qhc-appt-*`).

item.name: 6 Patient summary
item.description: Stretch, test case P-01. The Referral Server produces an AU Patient Summary (AU PS) document on demand with `Patient/[id]/$summary` (HAPI IPS module with the AU PS plugin). Seeded patients 01, 02, 04 to 07, 10 to 13 and 17 to 20 carry conditions, allergies, medications, procedures and results; the others return placeholder sections.

request.description: AU PS document for a seeded patient with history. The first call after a server restart can take around ten seconds.

exec: pm.test('required sections and seeded history present', () => {

request.description: A seeded patient with no clinical history: the required sections are still present, each with one generated 'no information' entry.

item.name: 9 Clean up
item.description: Deletes everything this run created, by id (the server refuses a conditional delete that matches more than one resource). Run it after a full pass. A 400 or 404 only means that item was never created or is already gone.
